business_scope.primary_industry_name: Physical Wholesale Brokerage of Marine Fuel Oil and Distillates

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (federal level; Canton of Zug recommended commercial seat; unified Swiss Code of Obligations company law)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Swiss Germanic-codified tradition; Federal Civil Code (ZGB/CC) and Code of Obligations (OR/CO), with FINMA regulatory overlay for financial and high-risk commercial activities)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Swiss Confederation and the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (BIT, signed 27 January 2009, in force 13 April 2010)
Free Trade Agreement between the Member States of the EFTA (including Switzerland) and the People's Republic of China (signed 25 September 2013, in force 1 July 2014)

Convention between Switzerland and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with Respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (DTA, signed 6 November 1990; amended by Protocol of 25 September 2013, in force 1 January 2019)
Switzerland-EEC Free Trade Agreement of 22 July 1972 (still in force for trade in industrial products, as extended to the European Union)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Arts. 620-699 OR (SR 220) on the Aktiengesellschaft; Art. 697j-697l OR (beneficial owner notification, 25% threshold); Federal Act on the Transparency of Legal Entities and the Identification of Beneficial Owners (SR 221.426, adopted 22 June 2023, transitional operative date); Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/GwG, SR 955.0, as in force 1 January 2023), arts. 2-12 and 9a; FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (GwV-FINMA, SR 955.201); Swiss Criminal Code arts. 305bis-305ter (SR 311.0); Embargo Act (SR 946.231) and SECO implementing sanctions ordinances; Federal Act on the Commercial Register (SR 221.41) and Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV, SR 221.411).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of each shareholder's and beneficial owner's passport (notarially certified in country of origin)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent civil registry authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Consular Legalization by Swiss representation for non-Hague-Convention countries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Handelsregisterauszug) of every corporate shareholder and of the ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Commercial Register / Companies Registry of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus certified German/French/Italian translation by a Swiss court-qualified translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney for incorporation and Swiss bank account opening (with UBO schedule)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin and, for Switzerland, Swiss notary co-signature
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization at the Swiss Embassy/Consulate in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Banker's reference and source-of-funds letter (KYC pack) from the relationship bank for the intended CHF 100,000 share capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing commercial bank (SWIFT-confirmed), with notarized statement on beneficial ownership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille/Hague notarization where the bank's state is not in the Hague system, otherwise SWIFT-authenticated letter accepted by the Swiss counterparty bank

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors and UBOs against (i) the SECO consolidated sanctions list and embargoes (Embargo Act SR 946.231), (ii) the UN Security Council consolidated list, (iii) the EU consolidated sanctions list as reflected in Swiss implementing ordinances, (iv) the OFAC SDN list as a bank and clearing-house benchmark for USD rails, and (v) domestic and foreign PEP databases per Art. 2(1)(a) AMLA and GwV-FINMA arts. 19-23; enhanced due diligence (EDD) applies because the entity is classified High_Risk_Special_License (physical wholesale brokerage of marine fuel oil and distillates) — international wire settlements via Standby LC/SWIFT require beneficiary-level sanctions screening, source-of-funds verification for all cash equivalents, and SECO prior authorization for transactions involving sanctioned persons or states.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: ZEFIX – Zentraler Firmenindex / Swiss Central Business Name Index (https://www.zefix.ch), operated by the Federal Commercial Register Office (Federal Department of Justice) with cantonal Handelsregisterämter as filing authorities
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Arts. 950-951 OR and the Commercial Register Ordinance (SR 221.411): the firm name must be true, lawful, distinctive, and non-deceptive; it must be expressed in an official Swiss language (German, French, Italian; Latin or Romansh variants permissible); non-Latin scripts (Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic) are transliterated into the Latin alphabet for the registered name, and any foreign-script version may be used only as an additional denomination, never as the registered statutory name; the mandatory legal-form suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft / AG / SA' must conclude the firm name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Eidgenössische/Bundes- (implies official federal status; refused for private companies)
Bank/Sparkasse/Börse/Fonds/Finanzintermediär (requires FINMA licence under the Banking Act or FinIA)
Versicherung/Assekuranz/Rückversicherung (requires FINMA licence under the Insurance Supervision Act)
Notar/Rechtsanwalt/Anwalt (protected legal professions; prior bar admission required)
Zug/Zürich/Bern and other cantonal or communal names (require approval of the concerned canton or commune)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name may be appealed within 30 days of the negative decision: the applicant files a written administrative objection with the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt), which transfers the case to the cantonal supervisory authority (in Canton Zug: the Handelsregisteraufsichtsbehörde / Verwaltungsgericht); further appellate review lies with the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) under the Federal Administrative Procedure Act (SR 172.021) and Art. 96 HRegV. The reservation is valid for 90 days and may be extended once for a further 90 days on payment of a renewal fee; filing an appeal suspends the contested reservation until final decision. A fallback name can be reserved in parallel and the application amended without losing the original filing date.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR), Articles 620–763 on the Aktiengesellschaft; Articles 640 and 652 on registration in the Commercial Register; Article 635 on minimum capital; Federal Act on the Commercial Register with implementing ordinances.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt), final review and entry via the Swiss Federal Commercial Registry Office (EHRA) in Berne.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation and the company statutes (Statuten), submitted electronically through the Swiss Commercial Register portal with certified notarial signatures.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The AG requires minimum share capital of CHF 100,000; at least 20% of the nominal value of each registered share, i.e. minimum CHF 20,000 in aggregate, must be paid in cash before registration, evidenced by a blocked-funds confirmation from a Swiss bank; no escrow account is otherwise separately imposed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The Subscribers ratify subscription of 1,000 registered shares, nominal CHF 100.00 each, total share capital CHF 100,000.00, and approve collection of the due minimum paid-in capital evidenced by the Swiss bank blocked-funds confirmation. RESOLVED: The registered office is established at Quai du Mont-Blanc 3, 1201 Geneva; the Board shall effect commercial register publication and regulatory notifications under Articles 640/652 OR. RESOLVED: [Name] and [Name] are appointed Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, respectively, with single/joint signatory powers. The Board is authorised to open bank accounts, appoint auditors, and procure all operating and stockpiling licences.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarisation of Incorporation Deed and Capital Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss canton notary public and the designated Swiss clearing bank holding the blocked capital deposit.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders execute the public deed before a Swiss notary, adopt the articles, specify the registered office, share classes, and board mandate. Simultaneously, the bank must issue a blocked-funds confirmation covering at least CHF 20,000 of paid-in cash. The notary authenticates all signatures and transmits the deed to the Commercial Register.
required_dossiers: Valid passports and birth certificates of all founders
Articles of incorporation signed by all founders
Bank blocked-funds confirmation for paid-in share capital
Registered office lease or consent of property owner
Appointment forms for the first board of directors and auditors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or bank queries the documents, correct the deficiency by amending the deed or providing supplementary board clarification within 10 business days; any defect in capital confirmation must be cured before resubmission to the Commercial Register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) serving the canton of Geneva.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the official incorporation application electronically through the cantonal registry portal. Include the notarised public deed, statutes, capital confirmation, officer identity documents, and a declaration that the directors are not subject to Swiss criminal disqualification. The registry verifies legal form, capital, and governing law compliance.
required_dossiers: Notarised public deed of incorporation
Company statutes
Bank blocked-funds confirmation
Board member and authorised signatory identity documents
List of shareholders and subscription statement
Signed affirmation of compliance with OR Articles 640/652
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues an order to regularise, submit an amended instrument or explanatory directors' resolution within 20 days; registry refusal may be appealed to the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority and thereafter to the Federal Administrative Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Entry in Commercial Register and Swiss Official Gazette Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Commercial Registry Office (EHRA) and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After cantonal approval, EHRA posts the company identification, capital, seat, statutes, and authorised signatories in the SHAB. The company acquires legal personality on definitive registry entry. The registry automatically issues the Swiss Company Identification Number (UID), and the tax administration is notified of the registration.
required_dossiers: Approved commercial register entry notification
Company UID assigned by EHRA
SHAB publication confirmation
Final certificate of commercial register entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication contains factual errors, immediately file a rectification request with the Commercial Register; any third-party objections to registered capital or seat must be resolved through judicial commercial court proceedings in Geneva.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Social Security, and Sector Licence Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), Geneva Cantonal Tax Administration, AHV/IV compensation office, and Swiss Federal Office for National Economic Supply (FONES), Mineral Oil Section.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the AG for VAT, direct federal tax, and social security with the competent compensation office. Simultaneously obtain a Swiss bank corporate account and execute the commodity trading compliance agreement. Apply to FONES for mineral-oil wholesale trader registration under the Federal Stockpiling Act before commencing brokerage of crude oil refined products.
required_dossiers: Commercial register extract and UID confirmation
Board authorisation for tax and bank registrations
VAT registration form for Swiss commodity trader activity
Social security AHV registration declaration
FONES wholesale mineral-oil trader application
AML/KYC corporate documentation for the Swiss trade finance bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or FONES applications are deferred, provide supplemental board resolutions explaining the planned wholesale brokerage model, confirm no unlicensed physical storage is performed, and submit missing AML/KYC beneficial-ownership declarations; adverse decisions may be appealed to the competent cantonal and federal administrative bodies within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Swiss Federal Office for National Economic Supply (FONES), Division for Mineral Oil; coordination with the Swiss Federal Office of Energy (SFOE) for energy product supervision.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Wholesale Mineral Oil Trader Authorisation under the Federal Stockpiling Act (Bewilligung zur Pflichtlagerhaltung für Mineralölprodukte) and licence to broker crude oil refined products in physical wholesale markets.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN), with cantonal environmental authorities for permit execution.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: No mandatory full EIA is required for pure wholesale brokerage; environmental license is limited to registration. Any incidental storage of marine fuel oil or refinery products above regulatory thresholds will trigger cantonal installation review and, where volume exceeds 10,000 m³, a full EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: All handling must comply with Swiss Waters Protection Ordinance, including no unauthorised wastewater discharge containing mineral-oil derivatives; VOC vapour recovery is required if tanks are regulated; FOEN emissions thresholds under the Swiss Clean Air Ordinance for NOx and VOCs apply on any energy auxiliary equipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and civil-defence clearance must be issued by the Geneva Cantonal Fire Prevention Service for the registered trade premises and any fuel-handling area; a structural integrity inspection is required for tank installations; occupational workplace clearance must be obtained from the Cantonal Labour Inspectorate and SUVA confirming compliance with Swiss occupational safety standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC), Schwarztorstrasse 50, 3003 Bern; Official Portal: www.estv.admin.ch; e-services portal: www.estv.admin.ch/eservices
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident foreign entity without a Swiss registered office or permanent establishment applies directly to the ESTV for Swiss VAT registration using the official form 'Registration as a taxable person (MWST/IVA/TVA)'. The application is filed electronically via the ESTV e-service or by post; the ESTV verifies the Unified Business Identification Number (UID - Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) register and issues a Swiss VAT/UID number bearing the suffix 'MWST'. The UID becomes legally effective upon notification; no personal appearance is required and a Swiss commercial register entry is not mandatory for a foreign entity without a Swiss branch. For a Swiss-incorporated Aktiengesellschaft (CH_AG), registration is initiated through the cantonal commercial register (Handelsregister), which allocates the UID; the UID is subsequently used for federal, cantonal, municipal and VAT filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope — An Aktiengesellschaft (AG/SA) is a mandatory entity-level taxpayer subject to federal corporate income tax on worldwide income with treaty relief, and to cantonal and communal profit and capital taxes that partially apply the territorial principle, exempting foreign permanent establishments and foreign immovable property. Pass-through treatment and US-style check-the-box classification are not available under Swiss law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No general entity-classification election exists. Available elections: (1) VAT-group election under Art. 13 of the Swiss VAT Act for closely interlinked economic, financial and organisational units; (2) tax-neutral restructuring rollover under the Swiss Merger Act (Fusion Act); (3) election to create untaxed replacement reserves on reinvestment of capital gains; (4) option for tax-privileged reserves and hidden-reserve build-ups permitted by cantonal practice; (5) hybrid mismatch: Swiss law applies mandatory anti-hybrid rules aligned with BEPS/MLI; no elective de-hybridisation mechanism is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / Imposta sul valore aggiunto)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual taxable turnover for Swiss-established businesses (Art. 10 para. 1 of the Swiss VAT Act). Non-established foreign suppliers are registrable without a de minimis threshold when they perform taxable supplies in Switzerland; voluntary registration remains available to recover input VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API-based pre-clearance, or digital stamping regime is in force. B2B e-invoicing is voluntary and predominantly Peppol BIS 3.0; public-sector invoices are processed via the Swiss e-Bill infrastructure and mandatory e-procurement channels. All Swiss-franc payment slips must display the Swiss QR-bill (QR-Rechnung) as of 30 June 2020. Swiss VAT returns are filed electronically through the ESTV portal and are subject to post-audit review rather than pre-clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated (Art. 23 para. 1 of the Swiss VAT Act) when the supplier proves that the goods left Switzerland or were delivered to an overseas consignee. Marine bunker fuel and ship stores supplied to seagoing vessels are zero-rated under Art. 23 para. 2 of the VAT Act. Services connected with exported goods, including freight, logistics, brokerage, and physical wholesale brokerage of crude oil and refined products, qualify for the 0% rate where the place of supply is abroad under the B2B place-of-supply rules (Art. 18 of the VAT Act) or where the services are directly and economically attributable to exported goods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic Swiss customs declaration and NCTS/EU transit document where applicable)
Transport and insurance documents, tank-farm warehouse receipts and delivery records evidencing physical removal
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Swiss customs and fiscal authorities retrospectively audit export substantiation; absent full and consistent proof, zero-rating is recharacterised as a domestic taxable supply and the exporter must remit Swiss VAT at 8.1% plus default interest. Fraudulent claims, forged shipping documents or inflated quantities constitute criminal offences under the Swiss VAT Act (Art. 87 para. 2 and Art. 94), punishable by administrative fines up to CHF 100,000 and criminal money penalties up to three times the evaded tax, with a 10-year limitation period for VAT evasion. Swiss exchange-control law imposes no separate statutory FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day timeline reflects the standard documentary credit and standby letter-of-credit (SL&C) cycle and banking due-diligence expectations in commodity trading, and a mere delay in repatriation does not by itself trigger a VAT clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Schweizerische Nationalbank, headquartered in Berne and Zurich, is the monetary authority and custodian of the Swiss franc (CHF); prudential AML governance and bank licensing supervision rest with the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) and the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF); Switzerland does not operate any exchange-control department, and the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (BAZG) administers only customs and embargo integrity, not currency surrender.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc is fully convertible with no distinction between current account and capital account transactions, consistent with the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Current Invisible Operations and Capital Movements; profit remittance to foreign shareholders is unrestricted and requires no SNB approval; dividends distributed maintain the statutory withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) at 35% unless refundable under an applicable double tax treaty or mitigated by the Swiss participation relief, which does not affect convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Switzerland imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation timeline for export receipts; the energy trading company may lawfully retain USD/EUR receivables and cash balances in Swiss or foreign bank accounts; only statistical monthly balance-of-payments reporting to the SNB is triggered for cross-border receivables and payables above the statutory threshold, without prior clearance or authorization.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Trade Finance Account
Operational Account and FX Hedging Collateral Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility as a primary treasury rail. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Revolut Business, Airwallex) are not Swiss licensed banks and cannot legally provide escrow, documentary credit, or commercial guarantee services for high-risk ISIC 4661 commodity trading; FINMA FinTech licences under Art. 1b of the Banking Act permit deposit-taking up to CHF 100 million only with plain, interest-free deposits and no securities custody or credit business, and the AML High_Risk_Special_License classification of an oil broker will trigger enhanced due diligence and almost certain rejection for core treasury clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for the founding directors and any beneficial owner holding at least 25 percent. FINMA Circular 2016/07 and the revised Anti-Money Laundering Act require personal identification before an account manager or Swiss notary public; at least the chairman and the CFO must attend an in-person compliance interview at the bank's Geneva, Zurich, or Lugano premises; purely remote video onboarding is not accepted for high-risk energy commodity traders, although a Swiss notary can act as a KYC conduit at the company's registered office.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership chain contains BVI/Cayman private trust company SPVs or a UBO with tax residence in an OFAC or FATF grey-listed jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Extract from the Swiss Commercial Register, full chain-of-control diagram with certificates of incorporation for every intermediate holding entity, FATCA and CRS self-certifications, tax residence certificates issued by the foreign tax authority, extract from the beneficial owner register of the offshore SPV, and a sworn UBO declaration excluding any politically exposed person status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commodity counterparty or vessel flagged under UN, SECO, OFAC, or EU sanctions, including shadow-fleet tanker associations for Russian/Iranian/Venezuelan crude
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions-screening certificates of all suppliers, buyers, vessels and brokers; IMO number with RightShip and Lloyd's List vetting record; purchase/sales contracts with INCOTERMS 2020 and bill of lading plus certificate of origin; SECO embargo circular compliance register; and a written environmental, social and governance supply-chain policy certified by the managing director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment instructions and split payments: contractual buyer or seller requests settlement to a different beneficiary or routes proceeds through two separate banks for one cargo
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed tripartite acknowledgment identifying the third-party lender or factoring intermediary, full SWIFT MT103 or MT202 COV cover with beneficiary account details, copy of the back-to-back purchase and resale contracts, anti-money-laundering declaration that no split payment will be executed for an oil cargo settlement above USD 250,000, and a breakdown of the receivables purchase assignment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Turnover-to-capital mismatch: first-year annual turnover materially exceeds the declared trading capital and relies on unsecured and foreign-parent intercompany loans
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited opening balance sheet, intercompany financing agreement with arm's-length interest rate, board minutes ratifying the working-capital facility, transfer-pricing documentation aligned with Swiss Federal Tax Administration Circular No. 6 on hidden equity rules, and evidence that the debt-to-equity ratio satisfies Swiss commodity-trader financing market conventions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections from the foreign parent must be credited to the Swiss AG operational account via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 COV for high-value payments) with ISO purpose code P12 'Inward direct investment' and a bank reference line stating 'contribution to CHF 100,000 fully paid share capital'. The custodian bank requires the notarised capital-increase deed registered in the Swiss Commercial Register within 30 days, the share subscription confirmation, and source-of-funds documentation proving the origin of the monies is neither tax evasion nor proceeding from sanctioned jurisdictions; no prior SNB clearance is required, only the statutory monthly cross-border balance-of-payments statistical survey if the filing threshold is surpassed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (i) marketable commodity settlements via SWIFT MT103 with ISO purpose codes P12/P13, cleared through SIX SIC for CHF and correspondent nostro accounts for USD/EUR; (ii) documentary commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600, sight or 30-90 days usance, confirmed for the first ten crude cargo purchases; (iii) Standby Letters of Credit under ISP98 issued by UBS Switzerland AG or BCV to guarantee supplier performance obligations; (iv) receivables collections via SWIFT MT202 COV and EUR payments cleared through TARGET2 using a euros correspondent; all rails require prior AML screening of the beneficiary and vessel/port confirmation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable FX forward contracts in USD/CHF, EUR/CHF and USD/EUR with tenors of one to twelve months, documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and cleared through the bank's treasury desk
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for settlement currencies of African crude-producing states (NGN, AOA, CDF) where the local foreign-exchange market is restricted or insufficiently liquid
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) converting USD-based floating-rate trade-finance funding into CHF or EUR fixed-rate exposure

Physically settled and cash-settled FX options, including call/put spreads, used strictly for hedging commodity trade receivables and payables and disclosed to SNB statistical reporting where materiality thresholds apply

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate tax return (federal direct tax, cantonal and communal corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal tax administration (jurisdiction of registered office) for the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; extension possible by the canton up to 30 September (Art. 125 DBG)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty up to CHF 10,000; default interest on underpaid tax; failure to file may lead to estimated assessment, administrative fines, and criminal sanctions for willful evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value added tax (VAT) return for quarterly or annual taxation of wholesale crude oil, marine fuel, and distillates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of each quarter; annual VAT summary and adjustment due by 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: FTA summary fine up to CHF 30,000; late payment interest at 4% per annum; suspension of VAT license for persistent non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AHV/AVS social security wage declaration for all employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse) and supplementary pension institutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the year-end; salary statements must be filed together with annual settlement of contributions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalty up to CHF 5,000; criminal prosecution for non-payment of withheld employee contributions; interest on arrears at 5%.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial register information confirmation and update of share capital, directors, UBO register, and registered office documentation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Register of Commerce (component of the district court)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Upon any change within 14 days; annual verification recorded in the AGM minutes kept at the registered office (no separate annual filing exists for unchanged AGs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update may render the registration ineffective against bona fide third parties; directors may face penalties up to CHF 50,000 and judicial dissolution in severe cases.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Full statutory audit required if the company exceeds two of three thresholds for two consecutive years: balance sheet total CHF 6 million, turnover CHF 12 million, 50 full-time employees. Smaller AGs may opt for limited review or be exempted if fewer than 10 FTE and below CHF 2M turnover. Wholesale petroleum trading, given its high-risk profile, typically undergoes a full audit as a matter of prudent governance.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss GAAP FER (ORM art. 957-962); IFRS mandatory for federally listed companies; financial statements must be prepared by the board within 6 months of year-end and presented to the shareholders at the AGM.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Swiss AML law, the board must keep a current register of beneficial owners at the registered office. At least once per year, during the AGM, the board confirms in minutes that the UBO register is accurate and reflects any share transfers. Any transfer altering the UBO register must be recorded within 30 days; the register is not publicly disclosed.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% Federal statutory corporate income tax on net profit (effective Federal rate 7.83% after deductibility of the tax itself); combined Federal + cantonal + communal headline rate for a trading AG seated in Zug approximates 14.6% effective, with a national effective range of roughly 11.9% to 21.6% depending on the canton of registered seat.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: (i) Participation exemption: 95% exemption of dividends and capital gains from qualifying participations of at least 10% or CHF 1,000,000 market value; (ii) Patent box: up to 90% deduction of qualifying IP income; (iii) R&D super-deduction: additional 50% deduction of qualifying R&D personnel and mandate costs (capped at 50% of the total tax base); (iv) Notional interest deduction on excess equity for financing and treasury functions; (v) cantonal capital tax optimization and advance tax ruling practice permitting TP margin certainty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined Federal/Cantonal Corporate Tax Return officially designated 'Steuererklärung für juristische Personen – Déclaration fiscale pour personnes morales' (SFTA model form), transmitted exclusively via the certified Swiss e-filing system SuisseTax or an approved cantonal portal (e.g., Taxware).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return must be filed within 6 months after the close of the fiscal year (Art. 124 DBG); for a 31 December year-end the base deadline is 30 June of the following year, with canton-granted extensions generally available up to 12 months; assessed tax is payable within 30 days of the assessment notice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 – Legal entity and UID identification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter UID number, commercial register FIRM data, legal form (Aktiengesellschaft), incorporation date, registered office, and board member identification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all non-resident beneficial owners and directors; attach powers of attorney; foreign UBO declarations are mandatory for AML review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1a – Net sales and brokerage commission revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross wholesale brokerage commission and trading margin from ISIC 4661 activities (marine fuel oil, distillates), including storage, service, and ancillary income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Commission earned as agent for non-resident principals must be reported as Swiss-source gross commission; advance pricing agreement or tax ruling should be attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 13 – Cost of goods and direct trading expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible purchase costs, freight, inspection costs, demurrage claims, and hedging costs matched to trading income; foreign exchange result declarations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All intercompany purchases from related non-resident traders must be arm's length and documented in the TP Local File; undocumented expenses are disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 15 – Personnel and social security expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Wages, bonuses, and AHV/UVG contributions, reconciled with payroll records and withheld-source tax statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Salaries paid to non-resident directors or specialists must be arm's length; compensation for board seats is subject to Swiss withholding at source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Decline in value of fixed assets applying tax-allowable depreciation rates (DBG Art. 62), reconciled with commercial accounts; no hidden reserve creation without disclosure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A: disclose any revaluation gains from internal restructuring separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income and cost on debt instruments and deposits; disclose shareholder loans tested against the thin capitalization ratio of 3:1 (debt:equity).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to non-resident parent must be at arm's length; excess interest is recharacterized as a constructive dividend triggering 35% WHT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net profit before income tax; the starting point for the federal and cantonal tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include transfer pricing adjustments and prior-year corrections; state currency translation into CHF at official exchange rates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset prior-year losses carried forward (maximum 7 years under DBG Art. 211) against current-year profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses must be evidenced by prior official assessments; no loss relief is available for a letter-box or shell entity lacking substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Where dividend income from qualifying participations is claimed as 95% exempt, attach a schedule of participations, holding periods, and minimum-equity proof.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exemption is unavailable for dividends from affiliated companies where the participation was acquired with non-arm's-length financing from non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annex TP-D1 – Transfer pricing documentation declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Formal declaration that Local File and, where applicable, Master File exist and are consistent with the arm's length principle; warrant availability upon request.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident related parties must provide benchmark studies and intercompany agreements in English; failure to provide triggers estimated assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of dividends and qualifying interest paid to non-residents, proof of 35% anticipatory tax deposit within 30 days of the due date, and any treaty refund filings made.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Form 823-B refund applications and PRC tax resident certificates; DTA relief is implemented by refund, not at-source exemption.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: reminder procedures followed by administrative disciplinary fine up to CHF 10,000 (Art. 174 DBG) and, where no return is filed, discretionary estimated assessment plus late interest at 4.5% p.a.; deliberate incompleteness or false entries trigger criminal tax evasion proceedings with fines up to three times the evaded tax (Art. 175 DBG) and imprisonment up to 3 years in aggravated cases.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss anticipatory tax (Verrechnungssteuer / impôt anticipé), which the distributing CH-AG must withhold and remit to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration within 30 days of the distribution date.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Under the Switzerland–PRC DTA (1990, as amended by the 2013 Protocol), the source-state withholding on dividends is reduced from 35% to 10% where the PRC beneficial owner is the recipient. Relief is implemented exclusively by refund: the Swiss subsidiary withholds 35%, and the PRC parent company files a refund application with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration on Form 823-B, annexing: (i) a tax residence certificate (TRC) for the relevant dividend year issued by the Chinese tax authorities, (ii) a legal entitlement declaration and ultimate beneficial ownership statement, (iii) documentary proof that the shareholding was held for the beneficial owner's own account and not as nominee, and (iv) Swiss payment confirmations. The claim must be lodged within three years after the dividend becomes due. For material recurring distributions, advance relief confirmation may be obtained through the FTA treaty-trust procedure; engagement of a Swiss tax attorney as collection agent is standard practice.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Swiss statutory WHT does not apply to royalties or to ordinary intercompany interest on commercial bank or shareholder loans; only bond or money-market instruments with 10 or more creditors attract the 35% anticipatory tax. The Switzerland–PRC DTA preserves a source-state cap of 10% on interest and 10% on royalties, which is relevant primarily for PRC-side source taxation of payments made by PRC counterparties to the Swiss entity. Caution: non-arm's-length interest or royalty payments are recharacterized as constructive profit distributions and become subject to 35% anticipatory tax with penalty exposure.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under the Swiss TP Documentation Ordinance (VPD, SR 651.703, in force from tax year 2020): Local File is mandatory where the taxpayer's annual aggregate gross value of transactions with related parties exceeds CHF 1,000,000; Master File is expected for multinational groups with consolidated revenue above CHF 50,000,000; Country-by-Country Reporting is mandatory where the group's consolidated annual revenue reaches CHF 900,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland has no formal Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) in the offshore sense, but the Swiss tax authorities apply the arm's length principle (Art. 58 DBG), statutory anti-abuse rules, and case law-based substance-over-form doctrines. A commodity trading or holding AG must demonstrate genuine economic activity: adequate qualified personnel, physical premises, independent risk management, and actual decision-making in Switzerland. Financing, IP-holding, and intermediary structures must maintain substance documentation (staff lists, board minutes, service agreements) to defend treaty access and avoid classification as a shell company; the LOB/PEP provisions of the Switzerland–PRC DTA deny treaty benefits where the enterprise's business is performed mainly outside its state of residence without genuine connection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Criminal Tax Evasion – Under-Declaration of Trading Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate filing of false, incomplete, or suppressed Swiss tax returns, including omission of brokerage commissions, use of unreported offshore booking centers, or false documentation of crude oil and refined product trades to reduce the CH-AG taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of up to three times the tax evaded (Art. 175 DBG) plus late interest at 4.5% p.a.; taxation by estimation at an increased rate; publication of final criminal judgments; in aggravated cases involving forgery, prosecution under Art. 186 DBG and Art. 146 StGB (fraud).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members and authorized signatories who knowingly sign defective returns face personal criminal fines, confiscation of personal assets, imprisonment up to 3 years, civil restitution to the tax administration, and disqualification from board office; travel alerts may issue during mutual assistance proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Constructive Dividend / Hidden Profit Distribution & WHT Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying expenses or consideration to non-resident related parties above arm's length (excessive management fees, non-arm's-length commodity margins, non-commercial interest) or distributing profits disguised as loans, thereby shifting profit to foreign shareholders and failing to withhold 35% anticipatory tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the excess amount as taxable profit and as a dividend subject to 35% WHT; the CH-AG is the debtor of the unwithheld tax; administrative fine up to CHF 10,000 and, in tax evasion cases, a criminal penalty up to three times the WHT evaded; interest accrues at 4.5% p.a.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors become personally liable for taxes withheld in fact but not remitted; individual criminal fines; personal seizure of assets; coercive imprisonment for failure to pay assessed penalties; per Art. 54 VStG rules, the creditors of the company may be joined in liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the CH-AG as a pure booking or mailbox vehicle with no employees, no office, or no risk function in Switzerland, interposed solely to capture Switzerland–PRC DTA benefits on commodity trading commissions, dividends, or interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief under LOB/PEP, full Swiss taxation of attributed income, 35% WHT on deemed distributions, withdrawal of favorable tax rulings, and fines for misleading authorities; the company may be struck from the commercial register if found to lack legal substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and UBOs face personal assessments on reattributed income, personal fines for false attestation of substance, criminal proceedings for aiding tax evasion, asset freezes and travel restrictions ordered in international concordat proceedings, and civil liability to shareholders and creditors for false representations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance / Missing TP Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare a Local File once related-party transactions exceed CHF 1,000,000, or maintaining manipulated benchmark studies, undocumented service fees, and intercompany financing inconsistent with the arm's length standard for crude oil and refined products flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Full discretionary TP adjustment by the tax administration with consequential tax and 4.5% p.a. interest; penalty fine up to CHF 10,000 for procedural non-compliance; for deliberately misleading TP documentation, penalty up to three times the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individual responsibility for signing the TP-D1 declaration; personal fines for false declarations; criminal exposure for certified tax advisers who knowingly prepared non-compliant documentation; director disqualification and personal restitution in group insolvency scenarios.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering Failure – High-Risk Commodity Trading
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct mandatory customer due diligence (KYC), failure to identify beneficial owners of counterparties in marine fuel oil trades, use of unverified standby letters of credit or shell-fronted intermediaries, and failure to file a Suspicious Activity Report with the Money Laundering Reporting Office (MROS) where oil-trading proceeds are suspected to derive from criminal activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine for the financial intermediary or merchant up to CHF 500,000 under Art. 37 GwG; FINMA enforcement action including prohibition from trading; criminal conviction under Art. 305bis StGB for money laundering with imprisonment up to 3 years (up to 5 years in qualified cases) and liability under Art. 305ter StGB for negligent failure to exercise due care; confiscation of profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and AML compliance officers named in criminal proceedings face personal fines, imprisonment up to 5 years for qualified money laundering or criminal organization participation, travel bans and pre-trial asset freezes, personal civil liability for losses caused, and disqualification from serving on any Swiss board.
